lessonTitle: Inflammatory Arthritis: Rheumatoid Arthritis, Gout and the Hot Joint

blocks.text: A 52-year-old woman tells you her hands are 'like wood' every morning. It takes her nearly two hours to be able to grip a kettle, and the knuckles of both hands are swollen and tender. She has been told twice that it is 'just wear and tear'. The difference between inflammatory and mechanical joint pain is the difference between a joint that can be saved by early treatment and one that is destroyed while everyone waits.

blocks.markdown: Joint pain has two broad mechanisms. **Mechanical pain** results from load on damaged cartilage and bone (for example osteoarthritis): it is worse with use and relieved by rest, with brief morning stiffness, bony swelling, crepitus and normal inflammatory markers. **Inflammatory pain** results from synovitis (inflammation of the synovial membrane): it is worse after rest and in the early morning, improves with activity, is accompanied by prolonged morning stiffness, soft or boggy joint swelling, warmth and often fatigue and systemic features, and the C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) may be raised. **Axial spondyloarthritis** is the inflammatory back-pain disease of young adults: insidious onset before about 45 years, lasting over 3 months, with early-morning and second-half-of-the-night pain and stiffness that improve with exercise but not rest. It is linked to sacroiliitis, enthesitis (inflammation where tendons insert into bone), anterior uveitis, psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, and to HLA-B27.

rows: Prolonged (usually over 30 minutes; often over an hour)
Worsens with use, better with rest
Often present, especially in the second half of the night
Usually on movement or when the joint is loaded
Rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthritis, crystal arthritis, septic arthritis
blocks.caption: Inflammatory versus mechanical joint pain.

blocks.title: Classifying joint pain
blocks.prompt: A 68-year-old man has right knee pain for 2 years, worse after walking and relieved by rest. Morning stiffness lasts about 15 minutes. Examination shows crepitus and bony enlargement, with no warmth. CRP is normal. Which pattern is this?

steps.text: Pain worse with activity and relieved by rest points to mechanical loading rather than synovitis.
Morning stiffness of 15 minutes is brief, below the 30 minute threshold typical of inflammatory disease.
Crepitus and bony enlargement without warmth are features of osteoarthritis, and a normal CRP argues against active inflammation.
Conclusion: a mechanical pattern (osteoarthritis). Management is exercise, weight management and analgesia; no urgent rheumatology referral is needed unless features change.

blocks.markdown: **Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)** is a chronic autoimmune symmetrical polyarthritis in which synovial inflammation (pannus) erodes cartilage and bone. It typically affects the small joints of the hands (metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints), wrists and feet (metatarsophalangeal joints), usually sparing the distal interphalangeal joints, with morning stiffness of over an hour. It is more common in women, is associated with smoking and carries extra-articular features (rheumatoid nodules, interstitial lung disease, scleritis, anaemia of chronic disease, cardiovascular risk). Joint damage occurs early, so patients with persistent synovitis should be referred to rheumatology urgently (ideally within a few weeks of onset).

**Investigations.** **Rheumatoid factor (RF)** is an antibody against the Fc portion of IgG: it is positive in many patients with RA but also in other conditions and healthy older people, so it has limited specificity. **Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies** are more specific for RA and are associated with erosive disease and may be present before symptoms. CRP and ESR indicate inflammation. Full blood count (normocytic anaemia), liver and renal function (baseline before DMARDs) and hepatitis and TB screening before biologics are needed. Radiographs may show soft tissue swelling, periarticular osteopenia and marginal erosions (late); ultrasound or MRI detect synovitis and early erosions. Disease activity is scored with the DAS28 (28-joint disease activity score).

**Treatment principles.** Treat early and aim for remission or low disease activity ('treat to target'). **Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs)** are started as soon as the diagnosis is made. Methotrexate is the usual first-line conventional synthetic DMARD, often with a short course of glucocorticoid to bridge until the DMARD acts. Other DMARDs include sulfasalazine, leflunomide and hydroxychloroquine. If disease remains active despite optimal conventional DMARDs, biologic agents (for example TNF inhibitors) or targeted synthetic agents are considered according to NICE criteria. NSAIDs and analgesics treat symptoms but do not alter progression. **Methotrexate is dosed once weekly** (not daily; daily dosing errors have caused deaths), with folic acid supplementation and regular monitoring of blood count and liver function; check the BNF and local protocol for doses and monitoring.

blocks.title: Reading serology
blocks.prompt: A 47-year-old woman has 4 months of symmetrical swollen tender MCP and PIP joints with 90 minutes of morning stiffness. RF is negative, anti-CCP is strongly positive and CRP is 38 mg/L. How do you interpret this?

steps.text: Clinical picture (symmetrical small-joint synovitis and prolonged morning stiffness) is highly suggestive of RA regardless of serology.
A negative RF does not exclude RA: RF is positive in only some patients, so seronegative-for-RF disease exists.
A strongly positive anti-CCP is highly specific for RA and predicts erosive disease.
A raised CRP confirms active inflammation. The diagnosis is RA; refer urgently to rheumatology to start DMARD therapy early, before irreversible erosions occur.

blocks.answer: RA is the likely diagnosis; anti-CCP is the more specific test, and early DMARD therapy is the priority.

blocks.markdown: **Acute monoarthritis: gout and septic arthritis.** An acutely hot, swollen, painful single joint is **septic arthritis until proven otherwise**, because untreated infection destroys a joint within days and can cause sepsis. **Gout** is a crystal arthritis caused by deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints in people with hyperuricaemia, typically presenting with sudden intense pain, redness and swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint, often after alcohol, dehydration, diuretics or acute illness. Serum urate can be normal during an acute attack, so the diagnosis is made by clinical picture and, when uncertain, by **joint aspiration**. The two conditions can coexist, and finding crystals does not exclude infection.

rows: Gout: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent urate crystals; culture negative
Rhomboid, weakly positively birefringent calcium pyrophosphate crystals
Often over 50 000, mostly neutrophils (can be lower)
Gram stain and culture may be positive; start treatment even if Gram stain negative
blocks.caption: Typical synovial fluid findings. Thresholds are approximate and must not be used to exclude sepsis.

items: Aspirate the joint before giving antibiotics if there is any suspicion of septic arthritis (do not delay antibiotics if the patient is septic).
Send fluid for Gram stain, culture, crystal examination by polarised light microscopy and cell count; take blood cultures.
If septic arthritis is suspected, give IV antibiotics per local policy and arrange urgent orthopaedic joint washout.
Acute gout: NSAID (with gastroprotection), colchicine, or a short course of glucocorticoid, according to comorbidity and renal function (check BNF).
After the flare, discuss urate-lowering therapy (for example allopurinol, started at low dose and titrated) with a target serum urate (NICE suggests below 360 micromol/L).

blocks.caption: Use to estimate how much urate-lowering therapy must reduce serum urate to reach the target.

blocks.title: Never assume gout
blocks.text: A hot swollen joint with fever may be septic arthritis even if the patient has known gout, and even if crystals are seen. Aspirate, culture and treat as septic arthritis until infection is excluded.

points: Inflammatory joint pain is worse after rest, with prolonged morning stiffness (usually over 30 to 60 minutes), soft swelling and raised CRP; mechanical pain is worse with use and relieved by rest.

RA is a symmetrical small-joint synovitis; RF has limited specificity, anti-CCP is more specific, and early DMARDs (methotrexate weekly with folic acid and monitoring) with treat-to-target prevent erosions.

Acute monoarthritis requires joint aspiration; gout shows negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals, septic arthritis shows a high neutrophil count and organisms, and sepsis must never be missed.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man has had low back pain for 6 months. It is worst in the early morning, wakes him in the second half of the night, and morning stiffness lasts 90 minutes; it improves with exercise and not with rest. Which pattern of pain does this describe?

distractorRationale.a: Mechanical pain worsens with use and improves with rest.
distractorRationale.b: Correct: night and early-morning pain, prolonged stiffness and improvement with exercise are inflammatory features.
distractorRationale.c: Neuropathic pain is a separate pattern and does not explain the stiffness and activity relationship.
distractorRationale.d: There is no visceral cause suggested.

questions.explanation: Prolonged morning stiffness, night pain and improvement with movement indicate inflammatory back pain, as seen in axial spondyloarthritis. Mechanical pain is the opposite: worse with activity and better with rest.

questions.stem: Which investigation is the most specific for rheumatoid arthritis?

distractorRationale.a: RF is positive in many other conditions and in healthy older people, so it is less specific.
distractorRationale.b: Correct: anti-CCP is highly specific for RA and predicts erosive disease.
distractorRationale.c: ESR is a non-specific inflammatory marker.
distractorRationale.d: ANA is associated with connective tissue disease rather than RA.

questions.explanation: Anti-CCP antibodies have high specificity for RA and may precede symptoms, whereas RF is sensitive but less specific. CRP and ESR are non-specific markers of inflammation.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman starting methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis asks about taking it. Which advice is correct?

options.text: Take it once daily with breakfast
Take it once a week on the same day, with folic acid supplementation, and have regular blood count and liver function monitoring
Take it only when joints flare
Take it with trimethoprim for infections without any concern

questions.correctOptionText: Take it once a week on the same day, with folic acid supplementation, and have regular blood count and liver function monitoring

distractorRationale.a: Daily dosing of methotrexate for RA is a dangerous error.
distractorRationale.b: Correct: weekly dosing, folic acid and regular monitoring are standard safety principles (check BNF and local protocol).
distractorRationale.c: Methotrexate works as a regular disease-modifying drug, not as a flare treatment.
distractorRationale.d: Trimethoprim interacts with methotrexate and increases the risk of bone marrow toxicity.

questions.explanation: Methotrexate is dosed once weekly, with folic acid and regular monitoring of blood counts and liver function. Prescribing and dispensing errors that lead to daily dosing can be fatal, and interacting drugs such as trimethoprim must be avoided.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man wakes at 3 am with a hot, red, exquisitely painful first metatarsophalangeal joint after a weekend of heavy drinking. He is afebrile and systemically well. Aspirated fluid shows needle-shaped crystals that are negatively birefringent under polarised light and no organisms on Gram stain. Which diagnosis is most likely?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals are monosodium urate.
distractorRationale.b: Pseudogout crystals are rhomboid and weakly positively birefringent.
distractorRationale.c: RA is a symmetrical polyarthritis, not an acute monoarthritis with urate crystals.
distractorRationale.d: Septic arthritis would show a purulent fluid and often organisms or systemic illness, although it must be excluded.

questions.explanation: Monosodium urate crystals are needle-shaped and negatively birefringent, identifying gout. Calcium pyrophosphate crystals in pseudogout are rhomboid and weakly positively birefringent.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman with a prosthetic knee has a hot swollen knee, temperature 38.9 C, and cannot bear weight. Her serum urate is normal. Aspiration shows turbid fluid with 80 000 white cells per mm3, mostly neutrophils, and some urate crystals. What is the best management?

options.text: Treat as gout with colchicine alone
Treat as septic arthritis: obtain cultures, start IV antibiotics, and arrange urgent orthopaedic washout

questions.correctOptionText: Treat as septic arthritis: obtain cultures, start IV antibiotics, and arrange urgent orthopaedic washout

distractorRationale.a: Crystals do not exclude infection; high cell count and fever indicate sepsis.
distractorRationale.b: Correct: septic arthritis is treated until excluded, even when crystals are present.
distractorRationale.c: Discharge risks joint destruction and sepsis.
distractorRationale.d: Steroid injection into an infected joint is dangerous.

questions.explanation: Fever, a very high neutrophil count and a prosthetic joint make septic arthritis likely, and crystals can coexist with infection. The joint requires culture, IV antibiotics and urgent orthopaedic drainage.

questions.stem: Morning stiffness lasting more than an hour that eases with activity is more typical of inflammatory than mechanical joint disease.
questions.explanation: Prolonged morning stiffness that improves with movement reflects synovitis and the inflammatory pattern. Mechanical disorders such as osteoarthritis produce brief stiffness and worsen with use.

questions.stem: A patient with gout has a serum urate of 540 micromol/L and a treatment target of 360 micromol/L. By what percentage must urate-lowering therapy lower the serum urate to reach target?
questions.explanation: Required fall = (540 - 360)/540 x 100 = 180/540 x 100 = 33.3 percent. Urate-lowering therapy is titrated step by step with monitoring toward the target (check NICE and BNF).

questions.stem: Contrast inflammatory and mechanical joint pain using history and examination, and give one example of each.
markingGuide: Inflammatory: prolonged morning stiffness (over 30 to 60 minutes), improves with activity, worse after rest, night pain, soft warm swelling, systemic features, raised CRP/ESR
Mechanical: worse with use, better with rest, brief morning stiffness, bony swelling and crepitus, normal inflammatory markers
Explain mechanism: synovitis versus cartilage and bone loading
questions.explanation: The mechanism, synovial inflammation versus mechanical loading, explains the opposite relationship with rest and activity.

questions.stem: Describe the typical clinical features and serology of rheumatoid arthritis and the principles of its treatment.
markingGuide: Symmetrical small joint polyarthritis (MCP, PIP, wrists, MTP), sparing DIP; morning stiffness over an hour; extra-articular features
RF sensitive but not specific; anti-CCP specific and predicts erosions; CRP/ESR raised
Radiographs: erosions and osteopenia; ultrasound or MRI detect early synovitis
Early DMARD therapy with treat-to-target; methotrexate first-line, short-term glucocorticoid bridging
Methotrexate weekly with folic acid and monitoring
Biologic or targeted therapy if inadequate response per NICE criteria; NSAIDs for symptoms only
questions.explanation: Early recognition and DMARD therapy prevent irreversible joint damage. Serology supports but does not replace clinical diagnosis.

questions.stem: Explain how you would distinguish acute gout from septic arthritis, and describe the synovial fluid findings that guide you.
markingGuide: Both present with a hot, swollen painful joint; septic arthritis is assumed until excluded
Gout: sudden onset, first MTP, triggers such as alcohol or diuretics, systemically well; serum urate may be normal
Septic arthritis: fever, systemic upset, inability to bear weight, prosthetic joint or risk factors
Aspirate before antibiotics: cell count, Gram stain and culture, polarised light microscopy
Gout: needle-shaped negatively birefringent urate crystals; septic: turbid, high neutrophil count (often over 50 000), organisms
Crystals do not exclude coexisting infection; treat as septic and arrange urgent orthopaedic drainage if suspected
questions.explanation: The decision rests on the combined clinical picture and joint aspirate. The consequences of missed sepsis are severe, so crystals alone never reassure.
